metadataReview.note: The Italian Ministry of Defence’s official chronology (Milite Ignoto, 1988, PDF p. 5; visually inspected) dates the whole Third Battle of the Isonzo to 18 October–4 November 1915. Correct the previous ending of 3 November by adding the final day. The opening date and location are unchanged. This chronology establishes the event bounds independently of CDB90 personnel estimates.

note:
Reviewed CDB90 match 298, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: Whole Third Isonzo battle, 18 October–4 November 1915. The Ministry of Defence official chronology explicitly supplies these complete bounds, extending the catalogue ending by one day rather than shrinking the event to accommodate a source phase. Visintin identifies the Italian Second and Third Armies and Boroević’s Austro-Hungarian Fifth Army throughout the first four Isonzo offensives. Retain the two Italian armies as one aggregate and the opposing Fifth Army as one local force. Both CDB strengths use code 3 (total personnel engaged); their original NAM, estimates and signed deviations remain unchanged. Identity and date review do not independently certify the numbers. Apply only after the staged metadata correction has been accepted. Identity review (attacker; original CDB90 name IT 2ND & 3RD ARMIES): Expand original CDB NAM to the historically identified field force; retain the original quantity, uncertainty and NAM qualifiers. The two Italian armies remain one aggregate; no individual army strengths are inferred. Identity review (defender; original CDB90 name AUS 5TH ARMY): Expand original CDB NAM to the historically identified field force; retain the original quantity, uncertainty and NAM qualifiers. AUS identifies Boroević’s Austro-Hungarian field army, not a present-day state.

The Italian Ministry of Defence’s official chronology (Milite Ignoto, 1988, PDF p. 5; visually inspected) dates the whole Third Battle of the Isonzo to 18 October–4 November 1915. Correct the previous ending of 3 November by adding the final day. The opening date and location are unchanged. This chronology establishes the event bounds independently of CDB90 personnel estimates.
